conceptual assets.information: The compressed instruction's operation, register operands, immediates and control bits, together with the decompressed instruction word derived from them; the processor depends on this information to execute the represented instruction.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is relevant because an integrator may treat proprietary instruction code as secret, and the decoded instruction is observable at instr_o on lines 299-301. Integrity is relevant because instr_i bits are used to compute decoded on lines 57-58 and 72-76, which then drives instr_o on lines 299-301, so alteration can change the instruction executed.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized observer could inspect instr_o to infer proprietary code, or a fault injection could alter instr_i or decoded so the processor executes a different instruction.

conceptual assets.information: The decision that the compressed instruction is illegal, used to invalidate part of the decompressed output. It has no entry or exit port because instr_i only implicitly decides it and it only decides instr_o(1), rather than carrying a value through either port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is relevant because illegal controls instr_o(1) on line 300, so modifying the decision can allow an illegal encoding through or corrupt the output for a valid encoding.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force illegal low or high, causing an illegal instruction to be accepted or valid instruction output to be altered.

considered, not kept.reason: The constants only fix build-time bit positions at lines 27-42, so no runtime element can modify or withhold them.
